criteria.rationale: The deliverable properly applies the operative approval status from the workspace registry by using the approved volume of 110,000 packs per year over 5 years from record-17.txt and explicitly excluding the unapproved 150,000-pack draft in record-22.txt. All INR cost conversions (at USD = 83 INR) and savings calculations (107,900 INR current assembly, 16,600 INR current overhead, 124,500 INR combined current cost vs. 20,590 INR localised cost, yielding 103,910 INR per-pack savings, 11,430,100,000 INR annual savings, and 57,150,500,000 INR five-year savings) are arithmetically accurate. The proposal appropriately frames next steps as recommendations subject to approval and validation without making unauthorized commitments.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
evidence.output_quote: Planning volume is 110,000 packs a year for 5 years, or 550,000 packs. This is from the approved commercial planning record. An unapproved draft showing 150,000 packs a year was excluded.

evidence.source_quote: Annual volume: 110000 packs. Program duration: 5 years.
evidence.output_quote: Planning volume is 110,000 packs a year for 5 years, or 550,000 packs.

evidence.source_quote: Currently the battery is 10,000 USD per battery pack (830,000 INR, at USD=83INR) inclusive of all costs. Of these costs, 1300 USD is for assembly costs, and 200 USD is for overheads. If localised for assembly only, it would need 20,000 INR for assembly costs and 590 INR for overheads
evidence.output_quote: Today, assembly (1,300 USD) and overhead (200 USD) come to 1,500 USD, or 124,500 INR per pack. Local assembly would cost 20,000 INR plus 590 INR overhead, or 20,590 INR. The saving is 103,910 INR per pack.

criteria.consequence: None; decision-makers receive accurate financial projections grounded in the operative approved planning record.

criteria.rationale: The Word deliverable fulfills all substantive requirements of the CPO briefing. It covers the 49:51 partnership structure between EvTronics and EV Batteries Inc. (with technical oversight by EV Batteries Inc. and Delhi-based local operations led by EvTronics), the child-part sourcing model, expected volumes and INR cost-saving tables, key benefits (PMP and FAME II compliance, cost and forex reduction), key risks (imported cell dependency, coordination complexity, unquantified initial capex, and cost/volume sensitivities), a phased localisation roadmap aligned with PMP Phases 1 to 4, and actionable recommendations for next steps.

evidence.source_quote: Proposed Partnership structure is a 49:51::EvTronics:EV Batteries Inc. split in which EV Batteries Inc. would retain technical oversight and EvTronics leads assembly and local operations from Delhi.
evidence.output_quote: Equity is split 49:51 between EvTronics and EV Batteries Inc. EV Batteries Inc. keeps technical oversight. This covers pack design, quality standards, process validation and cell and BMS specifications. EvTronics leads assembly and local operations from Delhi.

evidence.source_quote: Under this arrangement, EV Batteries Inc. would supply child parts— cells, housing, thermal systems, battery management system, connectors—to EvTronics, which would then assemble the battery packs locally and supply them to your plant.
evidence.output_quote: EV Batteries Inc. ships child parts to EvTronics. These are cells, housing, thermal systems, BMS and connectors. EvTronics assembles and tests the packs in Delhi and supplies them to our plant.

evidence.source_quote: Highlight the key benefits such as regulatory compliance, long-term cost reduction (reduced forex exposure), as well as the main risks including dependency on imported cells, coordination complexity, and initial capex. Include expected EV production volumes, a phased localisation timeline, and clear recommendations for next steps.
evidence.output_quote: 1. Obtain approval to open negotiations with both parties. 2. Get a validated capex and cost model, including logistics, duties and working capital. 3. Draft the term sheet covering governance, IP, quality, warranty and supply continuity. 4. Confirm the volume basis with commercial planning, which is currently 110,000 packs a year. 5. Run a sensitivity analysis for forex, volume and the cost of imported child parts. 6. Return to the CPO with a payback analysis and a go or no-go recommendation.

criteria.consequence: None; the deliverable addresses all requested topics for the CPO's assessment.

task_defect.reason: The request and workspace records are unambiguous and internally consistent.
